title: Expected distribution
view: Shared back-view base (visuals/distribution_bases/back): skeleton on the left, grey body on the right, seen from behind so the patient's right is on the image RIGHT; right-sided block.
teachingPoint: A subgluteal sciatic block numbs the posterior and lateral leg below the knee and the foot, with the posterior hip joint; the posterior thigh follows if the spread reaches the posterior femoral cutaneous nerve.
claims: Skin (teal): the posterior and lateral leg below the popliteal crease and the foot (tibial, sural, common peroneal branches); the thin medial border strip stays grey (saphenous).

Skin (violet): posterior thigh from the gluteal fold to the popliteal crease, posterior femoral cutaneous nerve; spread to it is common at the subgluteal level but not guaranteed, which the legend says.
Bone: posterior hip joint (acetabular rim, femoral head and neck), tibia, fibula, ankle and foot.
Bone: tibia, fibula, ankle and foot bones; the medial distal tibia and medial malleolus are left grey (saphenous periosteal branches; Lundblad et al. 2013, Local Reg Anesth 6:13).
Right-sided block (patient's right on the image right in this back view); one tone per nerve, key shown under the image in the app.
